text:
todd: Heads up — onboarding call with FinEdge tomorrow. They want a written guarantee for p99 300ms for short-chat queries (<128 tokens). Can eng confirm feasibility?

sam: short answer: probably yes for moderate QPS but tradeoff with throughput. p95 and p99 diverge a lot when KV cache is cold or microbatching is large.

maya: added profiling numbers from last load test: `single-token profile (kernel=a): p50=45ms p95=120ms p99=310ms` vs `kernel=b: p50=50ms p95=135ms p99=260ms`. Kernel B gives tighter tail but slightly higher median.

sam: kernel B uses different attention tiling and avoids some small-kernel launch overheads. It increases per-token compute but reduces tail variance.

jon: from product: FinEdge will accept slightly lower throughput if p99 is stable. They expect 99.9th percentile spikes to be rare. What QPS are we assuming?

todd: FinEdge target peak 300 qps, steady 100 qps.

maya: important: KV cache warmup pattern for their workflow is bursty with many cold sessions. Cold-KV causes p99 jumps due to rewarming and cache-miss path. In the last repro we saw KV-miss adds ~180ms on the critical path.

sam: options: 1) prioritize p99: smaller microbatch (1-2), kernel B, pre-warm KV for known customers; 2) prioritize throughput: larger microbatch (8-16), kernel A, rely on caching and autoscale.

carla: ops question — pre-warm KV automatically for a single tenant? that adds memory + some scheduling complexity. Is that supported?

maya: we have a customer-cache pinning prototype in staging. It allocates a KV slot per-tenant and keeps warm for a TTL. Tradeoffs: increases hotset and GC pressure.

sam: also saw a perf regression after the latest kernel swap on 2026-01-18: p99 for small inputs moved from ~250ms -> ~380ms on some machines. Root cause was an accidental microkernel path that fell back to host memcpy more often. We reverted, but we need guardrails.

perf-bot: load-test-2026-02-02: FinEdge-sim QPS=300, config: microbatch=8, kernel=A, kv-ttl=60s -> p50=60ms p95=130ms p99=420ms (tail correlated with KV misses and jittery scheduling)

jon: given that, product asks for a formal proposal with two SLAs: p95=150ms and p99=300ms for their steady workload. Can eng price impact and ops complexity?

sam: rough unit economics: switching to microbatch=1 and kernel=B increases GPU token cost by ~18% at steady QPS due to lower batching efficiency. Pre-warming KV for a tenant adds ~0.5-1GB effective memory reservation across nodes -> affects packing.

maya: mitigation techniques: - aggressive prefix KV caching for session templates - opportunistic background KV re-warm on session start - use kernel B for <128 tokens and kernel A for longer ones (dynamic kernel selection)

carla: dynamic kernel selection sounds neat but requires routing logic and validated compatibility across model quantizations. Ops work estimate?

sam: engineering estimate: 2 weeks to implement heuristics + canary, 1 week to extend console routing UI, + ongoing monitoring. Ops changes: one config flag and KV pinning toggle per-tenant.

jon: can we offer a conditional SLA: p95=150ms guaranteed, p99=300ms best-effort with credits if we miss >3x/month? That might be more acceptable to FinEdge and reduce engineering urgency.

todd: FinEdge will push back on anything "best-effort". They want hard p99 for their compliance team. But they are flexible on price.

maya: technical compromise: we can guarantee p99 during steady-state (after a 60s warm window for new sessions). We should call out cold-start exceptions in the contract — e.g., first 30s after a long idle or after a model swap.

sam: recommended runtime config to hit guarantee: kernel=B for short requests, microbatch<=2, KV pinning enabled for their tenant with kv-ttl=300s, and a canary rollout with perf tracing on 2 dedicated GPUs.

perf-bot: projected: with that config and QPS=100 steady, estimated p50=55ms p95=140ms p99=290ms and throughput drop ~12% vs baseline microbatch=8. (numbers based on replayed traces)

jon: that seems workable. Sales to propose: guaranteed p95=150ms and p99=300ms for steady-state with listed exceptions and a price premium for reserved capacity.

todd: will propose to customer. Action items: 1) sam/maya implement canary paths and kernel heuristics (est 2w), 2) ops enable KV pinning prototype for FinEdge tenant (config + capacity planning), 3) product/contract to draft SLA wording with cold-start carveouts.

sam: noted. I'll create an RFC and link perf traces.

maya: I'll attach the profiling gist and test plan to the RFC.

carla: ops will estimate memory/packing impact tomorrow.

todd: thanks all — @jon i'll loop you in once RFC is up so you can include numbers in the customer deck. :thumbsup:

jon: thanks. small follow-up: can we add a regression guard that auto-rollbacks kernel changes if p99 increases >10% on canary?

sam: yes, that's on the rollout checklist. We will set a p99 SLO and webhook to rollback if breached in canary.

perf-bot: note: ticket RN-4572 created for kernel-heuristics and RN-4573 for KV pinning.

sam: wrapping up — keeping expectation realistic: we can hit strong p99 but it costs either throughput, memory, or price. Need sales to pick which lever to use.
